plain_claim: Removing the occurs check, and changing nothing else, breaks soundness: on X =? Box X the variant returns [X ↦ Box X], which is not a unifier, no finite unifier exists, and unify returns none; and on (X, (X, (Y, Z))) =? (Box X, (Box Y, (Vec Y, Z))) it returns dupσ = [(1, Vec Y), (0, Vec Y), (0, Box (Vec Y))], whose list of bound variables is [1, 0, 0] (X is bound twice), and whose k-fold unfoldings of the two sides disagree at depth 2 for every k, so the depth-indexed solution property fails.
depth_justification: Evaluation of the algorithm on two inputs, a size argument for the absence of finite unifiers, and a case split on k for the unfoldings.
nonvacuity_witness: Counterexample; its instances are the witnesses.
non_claims: The second instance shows that the returned substitution fails the depth-2 test for every number of unfoldings; that the equations X = Box X, X = Box Y, Y = Vec Y have no infinite-tree solution at all is not proved here (no infinite-tree semantics is formalized).

The variable Z in the second instance is there to raise the fuel numVars from 2 to 3; without it the variant runs out of fuel and returns none on (X, (X, Y)) =? (Box X, (Box Y, Vec Y)) (run_needs_occurs_check_for_bound).

tier_justification: Solvability of first-order equations over infinite (rational) trees is classical (Huet 1976, Chapter 5; Colmerauer 1982; Courcelle 1983; Jaffar 1984; Martelli and Rossi 1984; Maher 1988). plain_claim: If unifyNoOC s t returns some σ and the left-hand variables of the returned association list σ are pairwise distinct (the run eliminated no variable twice), then for every depth n there is a number k such that σ applied k times to s and to t gives terms that agree at every position of depth below n; agreement up to depth n is preserved by applying any substitution; agreement of the k-fold unfoldings persists for every number of unfoldings m ≥ k; and on finite terms, agreement at every depth is equality.

depth_justification: The proof (ToyUnify/OccursCheck.lean) shows that agreement in the limit (LimEq) is an equivalence and a congruence preserved backwards by every pass, that in a run whose output is duplicate-free a variable bound to a variable never reappears (invariant ChainInv), so var-to-var chains in the output have length at most one, and that then 2n and 2n + 1 unfoldings agree up to depth n (eqUpTo_iterSubst_converge).

The distinctness condition is checked on the output; which inputs lead to double elimination is not characterized.
The existential k is not a bound on k (the proof yields k = 2n for the output's own bindings, but no bound for s and t is stated).
